mainEntity.name: I think I need a minor framing adjustment—what should I do first before I make it worse?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor framing adjustments usually mean small, targeted corrections to wall, floor, or ceiling framing so doors, windows, finishes, or structural alignment sit correctly. For a new issue, the safest first step is a site check to confirm whether the problem is cosmetic, load-related, or caused by moisture or movement. If the framing is supporting anything structural, do not cover it up before it is evaluated.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start with a site check to confirm whether the issue is cosmetic, structural, or moisture-related. Don’t patch over bowed, cracked, or out-of-square framing until it’s evaluated, because the fix may need reinforcement rather than a simple trim adjustment.
